CJP warns of nationwide protests Cockroach Janta Party's Abhijeet Dipke had earlier given an ultimatum of 5 p.m. local time for Union education minister Dharemendra Pradhan's resignation. He also warned the government of pan-India protests. By evening, CJP spokesperson, Saurav Das posted visuals of the protest showing the crowd and said, "Huge number of young people gathered at Jantar Mantar, peacefully!" Singapore blocks social media posts against Indian community The Singaporean government asked three social media platforms to remove 14 posts that targeted the Indian community and sough to "undermine" the country’s "model of multiculturalism." The police have issued disabling directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA) to block access to the posts on YouTube, Facebook and X, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said in a statement. Indians make up between 7% and 9% of Singapore's population of over six million. CJP protest at Jantar Mantar grows as hundreds join A large crowd of protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, where the satirical Cockroach Janta Party was demonstrating and demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan amid allegations of irregularities in recent exams. The protesters were seen wearing cockroach masks and holding up pamphlets calling for accountability. This movement began after India's Chief Justice, Surya Kant, reportedly likened young critics of the government to "cockroaches" and "parasites" during a court hearing, sparking outrage among young people. "It's about time we own it and come to the streets to show that, in fact, no, we are not lazy, we are here, and we are demanding change," Arushi, a student who gave only her first name, told DW. "India deserves better administration of crucial exams by the government," said 20-year-old Sarthak, who also gave only his first name, told Agence France Presse news agency. Last month, the nationwide medical college entrance exam was scrapped after investigators uncovered a question paper leak.
